newsitem.title: USA: Huang agrees conditionally to testify in U.S. probe.
newsitem.headline: Huang agrees conditionally to testify in U.S. probe.

text.p: John Huang, a key witness in the Senate probe of funding of President Bill Clinton's 1996 campaign, has agreed to testify if given limited immunity against prosecution, Sen. John Glenn said on Tuesday.

Huang, a former Commerce Department official who became an important Democratic Party fundraiser, would still be open to prosecution for treason, illegal disclosure of classified information, perjury and other charges, the Ohio Democrat said at the opening of the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee hearing.

The Democratic National Committee returned nearly $1.6 million in questionable funds raised by Huang. Another important fundraising figure, Charles Yah Lin Trie, a former Arkansas restaurateur and friend of Clinton, remains in hiding and is believed to be in China. He raised or donated $645,000 for Democrats which was later returned.
Committee chairman Sen. Fred Thompson, Republican of Tennessee, called for senators to continue opening remarks while the offer of Huang's testimony was explored.
Glenn, who reported the offer in his opening statement, said he wanted to discuss it with the Justice Department before making a decision on whether it should be accepted.

As he explained it, Huang would still remain open to criminal prosecution on a variety of charges if there were evidence he committed espionage, disclosed classified information or made false statements under oath.
